newsitem.title: USA: Alltrista gets $129 mln U.S. Mint contract.
newsitem.headline: Alltrista gets $129 mln U.S. Mint contract.

text.p: Alltrista Corp said Monday it was awarded a five-year contract valued at $129 million, based on current demand, to supply copper-plated zinc one cent coin blanks to the U.S. Mint.
As in the past, the zinc needed to produce the blanks will be provided by the U.S. Mint and therefore is not included in the estimated contract value, it added.

Alltrista also said its board authorized the repurchase of up to 200,000 shares of outstanding common stock. Last week, the company said it had completed the repurchase of 430,000 shares under an earlier approved program.

The U.S. Mint contract calls for a target volume of 30 truckloads of coin blanks per week for delivery to the Denver and Philadelphia mints with volumes adjusted each quarter, based on demand, Alltrista said. The blanks will be produced at its facility in Greeneville, Tenn.

"Our zinc products operation has been producing one cent coin blanks for the U.S. Mint since December of 1981," Thomas Clark, president and chief executive officer, said in a statement. "The significance of this contract, however, is that it is for a five-year period. Other contracts have had an initial term of one year."
He added the manufacturing of zinc one cent coin blanks in the United States began in late 1981 when the cost to produce a copper one cent coin was approaching he purchasing power of the coin.

Alltrista performs all manufacturing steps to produce finished blanks, including melting, continuous casting and rolling of the zinc strip. Blanks are produced from the strip, rimmed and copper plated. The blanked coins are then shipped to the U.S. Mint where the final coining step takes place.
